title: Email Platform Costs: Compare Your Actual Workload
author: Stefan Bogdanescu
excerpt: Email services use different billing units: contacts, active subscribers, sends, seats or combinations. Read your own plan, including which contacts count, overages and cancellation terms. Do not assume every provider charges the same way.
content:
Start with your current plan

Email services use different billing units: contacts, active subscribers, sends, seats or combinations. Read your own plan, including which contacts count, overages and cancellation terms. Do not assume every provider charges the same way.

Model the same workload

Compare the same list size, sending volume, retention, integrations and support needs. Use current vendor prices rather than a made-up industry average. Include migration and training time on both sides.

Include the self-hosted costs

Servers, mail delivery, storage, backups, monitoring, patching and staff time belong in the calculation. Local AI may remove a provider's per-token invoice while adding compute demand. A server already running can still need an upgrade.

Find a break-even point, not a slogan

Build a small worksheet with your current workload and a growth scenario. Label assumptions and revise them after a measured pilot. The useful result is the cost and responsibility profile that fits your team, not a universal claim that self-hosting is always cheaper.

Sources and scope

Configuration and test results determine the behavior of an individual installation. This guide does not certify a live deployment or promise a cost, deliverability or compliance result.
